questions.question: Why does CSS block rendering, and what is critical CSS?
questions.answer: The browser must build the CSSOM before painting to avoid a flash of unstyled content, so stylesheets block render. Critical CSS inlines the above-the-fold styles and defers the rest to speed first paint.

questions.question: How do you find and reduce unused CSS?
questions.answer: Use DevTools Coverage to see unused rules, split CSS by route/component, remove dead selectors, and minify. Safelist dynamic class names before purging.

questions.question: What does will-change do, and why is permanent use bad?
questions.answer: It hints that a property will change, letting the browser promote/prepare the element. Permanent use consumes memory and GPU resources, so apply it before an interaction and remove it afterward.

questions.question: Why are transform and opacity cheaper to animate?
questions.answer: They can be handled in the composite stage without layout or paint. Animating width/height/top/left forces layout and often paint on every frame.

questions.question: What is layout thrash and how do you avoid it?
questions.answer: Repeatedly reading layout (offsetHeight, getBoundingClientRect) then writing styles forces synchronous reflow. Batch all reads first, then all writes, or use requestAnimationFrame.

questions.question: Defer a non-critical stylesheet without blocking render.
questions.answer:
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/app.css" media="print" onload="this.media='all'" />
<noscript><link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/app.css" /></noscript>

questions.question: Why can content-visibility:auto cause scrollbar jumps?
questions.answer: Offscreen elements are skipped and have no size until rendered, so the scroll height changes as they enter the viewport. Provide contain-intrinsic-size to reserve an estimated size.

questions.question: Why can a purge tool break a working UI?
questions.answer: It removes classes it cannot see in source, including dynamically constructed names (e.g. `text-${color}`). Safelist dynamic patterns or avoid runtime string construction.
